rationale:
bugs_open/393, both halves resolved. The bug: the no-change completion gate (gate 1b) writes a durable row — error_code NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT — whenever it cannot read a completing handler's result and the type's policy is abstain, and NOTHING reads that row. A handler whose result shape drifts is permanently exempt from grading, silently; the first instance (11 rows, all dark_section_audit, 2026-08-14→17) sat unread for 11 days, was found by a census accident, and its rows then start dying on the retention clock. The owner commissioned a reader (decision 4, 2026-08-25).

PART A ("fix the one known instance") DISSOLVED ON MEASUREMENT, and the measurement is in the lane NOTES with its queries. All 39 dark_section_audit items ever (live UNION archive) were read: the 11 unreadable events split exactly as the gate's own roster comment records — 7 were SPAWN RECORDS stored as the item's result (bugs_closed/287, fixed and rolled v1.0.1307 on 08-17), the rest were color-variable-fixer's foreign shapes, retired when the owner rerouted the type to css-patch-agent on 08-19. The roster entry is LicenceVoided with both carriers enabled=false, so nothing reaches it; and the type's NEW traffic (six rows filed the night of 08-25) is deliberately not dispatched — RFC_056 filing_mode=record, deferred with no handler and a release recipe in the spec. Nothing can complete, so nothing can complete ungraded. The roster's stated precondition for re-enabling ("re-measure css-patch-agent's reply shape on THIS type") cannot be satisfied: that handler has ZERO completions of the type to measure. The perishable evidence (full messages + context of all 11 rows) was extracted to the lane directory FIRST, before any of this, because the retention clock was already eating it.

PART B (the commissioned reader) IS THIS SUBMISSION. A new mode in cmd/config-key-audit — the estate's ratchet home, in council scope by the 2026-08-23 widening — modelled line for line on --commit-sha-exposure:

* `--ungraded-completions [--acks <file>] [--report]` groups the code's rows by context->>'item_type' (the writer stamps it into context; the bug file's own query regexed error_message because it had not confirmed context — the clean key is used here, and a context-less row COALESCEs into its own visible group rather than being dropped).
* Any type not acknowledged in no_change_unreadable_acks.json FAILS the run (exit 1). An ack needs a non-empty `reason` — a hollow ack is warned about and ignored — and the file ships INSIDE the image from committed HEAD (the commit_sha_exposure_acks rule), so an unreviewed acknowledgement is unrepresentable.
* dark_section_audit is acknowledged at birth with its full diagnosis attached, and the ack's text warns that the type reappearing after its held rows are released is the roster comment's precondition coming due — do not re-acknowledge without doing that work.
* THE ALIVENESS CONTROL, which is the design's load-bearing subtlety: zero rows of the CODE is the HEALTHY state (the refuse-policy arm never reaches the record, so every row is signal), unlike the sibling checks where an empty population means blindness. So vacuity is guarded one level down: an agent_error_log that reads as EMPTY (hundreds of rows a day live in retention) is a blind read, refused with exit 2, never reported clean. The stdin shape REQUIRES the aliveness total (a pointer field, so a payload omitting it is distinguishable from a zero) — the wrapper builds it.
* --report writes ONE doc_notes row per run, clean runs included, body stating SCOPE ("11 rows across 1 type in a 49,046-row table") not just verdict — the family's pinned rule.
* Daily CronJob at 07:35 UTC — the slot chosen against the REPO census (grep of committed manifests), not `kubectl get cronjobs`, per finding-code-registry-check's stated rule; verified only my own manifest holds it.
* The finding-code registry entry flips human-evidence → consumed with reader/reader_sink IN THE SAME COMMIT, exactly as its own `why` field says to; TestShippedRegistryIsSelfConsistent (DBG-075's arm) is green with the flip — the reader file names the code as a same-file const (the LINK_CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE precedent).

PROVEN BEFORE SUBMISSION, at the wire not just in units: the live hand-run returns 11/1/acknowledged/exit 0 over a 49,046-row table; a synthetic novel type through the same emit path exits 1 with the remedy text; a zero aliveness total refuses with exit 2. Three ratchet guards mutation-proven (ack-always-true → novel arm reds; ack-lookup-dropped → acked arm AND the hollow-ack CONTROL red; hollow-ack-accepted → its test reds), file restored byte-identical.

Registered as DBG-077 (entry + index row) in the same commit, per the platform-seams ruling.

Part A of the bug dissolved on measurement (recorded in the bug file and lane NOTES), so no gate or handler code changes.

edits.rationale: The mode, modelled line for line on commitshaexposure.go: same acks-loader contract (missing file = exit 2 never an empty ack set; hollow reason warned and ignored; _-prefixed doc keys skipped), same two routes (direct Postgres under PG_CLIENTS_HOST for the CronJob, stdin object for the hand-run wrapper), same ONE-doc_notes-row-per-run rule. The decision (markAcknowledged) is a pure function split from the fetch so both directions are testable on one fixture. The groups query keys on context->>'item_type' and COALESCEs a context-less row into its own visible group — a row this reader cannot attribute is a finding about the writer, not a row to skip.
edits.sketch:
const ungradedCompletionsCode = "NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT" // same-file const: the registry checker verifies the reader FILE names the code
const ungradedGroupsQuery = `SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(t),'[]'::jsonb) FROM (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(context->>'item_type',''),'(no item_type in context)') AS item_type, count(*) AS rows, min(occurred_at)::text, max(occurred_at)::text FROM agent_error_log WHERE error_code='NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1) t;`
if errorLogRows == 0 { refuse, exit 2 } // zero rows of the CODE is healthy; an empty TABLE is a blind read
graded := markAcknowledged(groups, acked); if unackedUngradedCount(graded) > 0 { os.Exit(1) }

plan.risks:
1) EXPECTED OBJECTION — 'part A is closed by argument, not by a fix.' Deliberate, and the argument is measurement: nothing can currently complete ungraded (entry voided, carriers off, new traffic filing_mode=record with no handler), the historical population is fully attributed to two already-fixed/retired causes, and the roster's own precondition for any future re-enable is unsatisfiable today (zero css-patch-agent completions of the type to measure). The bug file gains a dated section saying exactly this; if the council wants a shape fix anyway, there is no live shape to fix it against.

2) The acks file is a silencing surface. Bounded the same three ways as its siblings: it ships from committed HEAD inside the image (an unreviewed ack is unrepresentable), a hollow reason does not count (mutation-proven), and the _doc plus the check's own remedy text both state that acknowledging an undiagnosed type defeats the mechanism.

3) The check is INERT until the next fleet release builds and applies it (RELEASE_IMAGES/AGENT_DEPLOY_SERVICES registration is in this commit; releases are whole-fleet, owner-run). Until then the hand-run wrapper covers it. Stated rather than hidden; the register entry says 'rides the next fleet release'.

4) doc_notes subject_key 'ungraded-completions' is new; nothing consumes doc_notes rows by that key yet — same standing posture as every sibling check (the row exists so a missing row can mean 'job did not run').

5) The aliveness control couples this check to 'agent_error_log is never empty in practice' (findingcodes.go's own premise). If a future retention change ever empties the table legitimately, the check goes exit-2 loud, not silently green — the safe direction, and the refusal text says what to look at.

6) go run collapses exit codes in the hand-run wrapper — documented in the wrapper itself per the family's landmine; the CronJob path runs the binary directly and is unaffected.
